explanation: No single shared feature. It fires on mid-compound or mid-name pieces in very mixed contexts: Android/code identifiers (layout_constraint, android.content.Context, @+id), technical phrases ('dependency injection', 'focus group', 'Manifest Destiny'), brand/name fragments (Deloitte, Odoo, velcro), and occasional function words. Activation is hard to predict from the token alone.

Mixed. Recurring themes are the word after a document-opening formula, such as 'Created/Written [by]', 'writing [to]', 'contact [us]', 'send comments [to]', and legal-opinion openers like 'This [appeal]', '[Name] [appeals]', 'BACKGROUND'. The rest is scattered medical-term pieces (dialysis, nystagmus) and citation digits.

Fires on subword pieces in the middle of rare or foreign proper names and words (Chandrababu, Voivodeship, Mihaly, Kravitz, Desrochers) and in foreign-language or technical words (Dutch, Italian, Albanian, biochemical terms like monoclonal, aglycones). It does not fire on ordinary English whole words; the trigger is a word being broken into unfamiliar fragments.

Fires on punctuation and function words inside formal, archaic or boilerplate prose: quoted scripture speech (commas, '?', '!', 'of' in Bible/Qur'an quotations) and patent-background phrasing ('technology of [the] present invention', 'Field of the In[vention]', 'device of [the] type'). It is weak in ordinary modern prose.

Fires strongly on 'to' in expressions of not knowing how to do something ('I have no idea how [to]', 'not sure how [to]', 'is there some way [to]'), mostly in help-seeking Q&A. Smaller offshoots: the syllable 'az' (Waziristan, Spazigaster), 'of' after 'the ways', and 'Berlin' after 'West'.

Fires on Japanese names and Japanese-related text: kanji or romanized pieces of Japanese personal names (Kazunori, Tamura, Kimura), anime/manga titles, and the number slot after 'No.' in Japanese patent application citations. It is weak on other East Asian or unrelated names.

Strongest on the preposition in fixed collocations: 'referred [to] (as)', 'with respect [to]', 'effect [on]', 'multiple [of]'. It also fires on mixed technical tokens (Frontend, emulsifying, cathode, ComboBox, URL). The preposition part is coherent; the rest is scattered.

Fires on a broad mix: conjunctions like 'and' and 'in' joining two clauses or items in informal or technical questions, pieces of names (Silesian, Deportivo, Dailymotion), URL and code separators ('::', '-best'), and others. I found no single unifying feature.

Fires on words about sleep and bedtime: 'sleep', 'sleeping', 'go to sleep', 'put her [to] bed', 'bed', 'night', 'snuggled'. It is moderate on lodging and rest words (hotel room, rooms, accommodation, home, rest). It is unrelated near zero.

Fires on number tokens, especially the second digit of a number or a spelled-out number, in duration, age or date quantities ('over a [three]-year period', '2[7] month period', '2[6] years old', '2[6] March', '3[6]0 degree'). It also fires on a few legal-brief tokens (PER C-URIAM, 'were on the brief').

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that is split into several tokens, mostly in non-English European text (French, German, Portuguese, Romanian, Danish, Spanish), such as 'déf'-endre, 'sp'-üren, 'ap'-arentemente and 'P'-elo. It also fires on similar word-initial fragments in English (Sk-ins, sm-ashes). Whole common words do not trigger it.

Fires very strongly on 'of' in the patent section heading '2. Description [of] (the) Related/Prior Art'. Related offshoots are 'by' in 'Written [by]' and tokens in legal case headers (dates, initials). It is weak elsewhere.

Fires on the token right after a completed operand or item in a structured list or expression: the operator after a function term in math problems ('-5*j(s) [-]', 'j*v(b) [+]'), the comma after a patent application number before 'filed', and 'and' joining two named entities. Assorted other tokens (writer, onto) fire too.

Mixed. It fires on surname pieces in judge lists ('MART[IN]', 'ELLI[OTT]'), 'am' in 'What [am] I doing wrong', 'of' in 'the X [of] Y' or 'of all the', closing parentheses and line ends in code or license comments, and assorted others. There is no clear common thread.

Moderate, broad firing on clause-continuation tokens after a noun phrase ('which', 'such (as)', 'where', 'and', '(') and on line starts and spaces in software license or copyright header comments. The top example, 'radar [systems]', stands out. The pattern is diffuse.

Fires on function words and subword pieces in Romance-language text, especially Spanish, Portuguese, French and Romanian prepositions and articles ('de', 'à', 'a', 'no'), and word-internal pieces such as Mec-án-ica. It also fires weakly on capital 'A' or 'G' at the start of names or acronyms in English (the A's, A-Team, GABA).

Fires on an opening square bracket '[', especially one that starts a citation or reference (\[[@B1]), a chemical or isotope label ([3H], [18F], [Fe(CO)]), or a bracket in code or regex. It is weaker for brackets used in plain array indexing.

Fires on the object or verb that refers back to an action or task already mentioned: 'do [this]', 'have to [do] his job', 'what I have [done]', 'the same [thing]', 'this [job]/[process]', 'time and [effort]', 'spending more [money]'. Context about doing or accomplishing a task matters.

Fires most on 'the' and 'of' in software license boilerplate ('Neither the name [of]', 'See [the] License', 'must reproduce [the] above'). It also fires on assorted tokens elsewhere (details [of], whether, '{', code punctuation).

Weak, scattered firing on subword fragments within abbreviations, URLs and identifiers: legal reporter citations ('A[.]2d', 'Fed.'), all-caps legal headings (COMPLA-INT, O P I N I O N), foreign-word pieces, and code tokens. The top example is a URL path fragment. There is no clear theme.

Fires on the conjunction or connector inside a compound name or fixed pair: 'Evaluation [and] Research', 'Cooley [&] Allen', 'his [or] her', 'and/or', 'permissions [and] limitations', 'briefs [and] appellate record', and 'including' in license text. It is moderate on other list continuations.
